government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental, Philippines
government.short_title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental…
government.plain_summary: This research highlights that while investing in mangrove restoration in Davao Occidental has been significant, outcomes have varied widely due to issues like incorrect species selection and lack of monitoring. Studies show that by matching the right species to each site and diversifying plant types, survival rates can be very high at over 95%. However, these effective methods are not consistently used because there's no unified policy framework. The study suggests creating a standardized governance system that mandates correct species use, promotes diverse planting strategies, and establishes community monitoring systems supported by partnerships between local governments and universities.

government.title: Machine Learning for Job Matching, Skills Mapping and Labour Market Forecasting in e-Government Systems
government.short_title: Machine Learning for Job Matching, Skills Mapping and Labour Market Forecasting in e-Governmen…
government.source: Journal of Applied Science, Information and Computing
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how advanced machine learning techniques could improve job matching and forecasting in e-government systems used by the Tanzanian government. The main challenges identified were poor usability of the system, weak job skill matching, and lack of real-time updates. Machine learning models helped analyze data better for these issues. The research found that integrating ML into these systems can significantly enhance decision-making, increase efficiency, and match workers with available jobs more accurately.

government.title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implications of Autonomous Weapons Systems
government.short_title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implicat…
government.source: European Journal of Law and Political Science
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how new technology like AI is changing international laws for wars. As weapons get more automated, it raises questions about who should be held responsible when they make decisions. The main idea is that current rules are still useful but need updating to fit with these new types of weapons. It suggests ways to improve the existing laws so that people in war zones can continue to rely on protections like not harming civilians unnecessarily.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.plain_summary: Political corruption is a big problem that governments often struggle with and sometimes use anti-corruption measures against their own democracy. International Anti-Corruption Commissions (IACCs) help address this issue by working with both international experts and local people. Some IACCs have more independence than others, which can affect how effective they are in fighting corruption. In places like northern Central America, when there are coalitions that include government insiders and activists at the table during negotiations, these groups use their influence to make sure anti-corruption efforts don't undermine democracy too much.

government.short_title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.source: Journal of Business and Econometrics Studies
government.plain_summary: This paper looks at corruption in Africa by examining how it affects governance, democracy, and mental health. It suggests that corruption is not just a legal issue but also stems from deep social and moral problems left over from colonial times. The study proposes solutions like strengthening institutions, developing ethical leaders, empowering citizens, and using restorative justice methods. By doing this, they aim to improve people's well-being and strengthen democratic systems in Africa.

government.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.short_title: Data Science as a Catalyst for Audit Transformation
government.plain_summary: Data science has become crucial as we generate vast amounts of information daily. It helps transform this data into useful insights for better decision-making across various sectors. For audit institutions, integrating data science can enhance their ability to manage public funds more effectively and improve accountability. By using data science, audits can provide clearer and more accurate reports that recommend improvements faster, which benefits the overall administration and improves citizens' quality of life.

government.title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.short_title: Killer Robots – A Case for SAIs
government.plain_summary: This paper discusses a scenario where autonomous killer robots are used in warfare without human intervention. These robots can make decisions about who to target based on AI algorithms trained to recognize certain uniforms. If one of these drones targets and kills an enemy soldier who is surrendering, it would violate international laws. Another concern is if the robot makes a mistake by attacking another similar system, leading to unintended conflicts.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a mediator
government.short_title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a m…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how ethical leadership can reduce corruption among public employees in Pakistan. It found that when leaders are ethical, it leads to higher job satisfaction for their staff. Higher job satisfaction then reduces the likelihood of corruption by making workers feel more committed to serving the public. This study suggests that if managers promote ethical behavior and boost employee happiness, they can help prevent corrupt practices in government.

government.title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democracies
government.short_title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democra…
government.source: African Journal of Law Political Research and Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how AI can help spot fraud in government spending in countries that are just starting to have democratic systems. It suggests that using AI like machine learning could make it easier for people to see if money is being spent unfairly or wasted. However, there are still big challenges like not having enough good data or fair rules. The main idea is that while AI can be useful, it needs to work with human checks and balances to really help stop corruption.

government.title: A Dual-Track Asset Recovery Model: Optimizing the Posthumous Forfeiture of Corruption Proceeds
government.short_title: A Dual-Track Asset Recovery Model: Optimizing the Posthumous Forfeiture of Corruption Proceeds
government.plain_summary: This study proposes a dual-track system for recovering assets from corrupt individuals who have died. Under this model, legal actions can proceed independently whether or not the person involved is still alive. This bypasses issues where criminal proceedings are halted due to death, which allows corruption proceeds to dissipate over time. By separating these processes, it ensures that law enforcement can quickly recover assets and maintain public trust in their work.

government.title: Policy Reconstruction in Combating Petty Corruption: Towards Progressive, Economic, and Utilitarian Justice
government.short_title: Policy Reconstruction in Combating Petty Corruption: Towards Progressive, Economic, and Utilit…
government.plain_summary: This study discusses how Indonesia can better handle small-scale corruption cases that don't cause significant financial damage but still harm the government's resources. Currently, these cases often go through formal legal processes which end up costing more than what was lost. The research proposes a new model called Progressive-Economic-Utilitarian Justice to address this issue. This model suggests making changes in how punishments are given and allowing some corruption cases to be handled differently using restorative justice methods.

government.title: Recalibration of Authority in Handling Corruption Crimes after Law Number 20 of 2025: A KPK-Centered Investigation and Prosecution Model
government.short_title: Recalibration of Authority in Handling Corruption Crimes after Law Number 20 of 2025: A KPK-Ce…
government.plain_summary: After Law Number 20 of 2025 was enacted, there's a challenge in deciding who handles corruption cases. The Police, Public Prosecution Service, and KPK all have their own authority under new laws. While this helps fight corruption, it can lead to overlapping work and conflicts between these groups. This study suggests making the KPK responsible for investigating and prosecuting corruption crimes, centralizing that function within them.

government.title: The Qualified Mens Rea Model: Layered Culpability in General Commodity Smuggling Offenses Implicating Corruption
government.short_title: The Qualified Mens Rea Model: Layered Culpability in General Commodity Smuggling Offenses Impl…
government.plain_summary: This research discusses challenges in proving criminal intent for general commodity smuggling cases linked to corruption. Traditionally, courts focus on individual mental states but modern economic crimes often involve corporations or government entities. The study proposes a new model called the Qualified Mens Rea Model that evaluates culpability across different layers including subjective intentions, corporate functions, and corruption-specific factors. This layered approach helps in distinguishing between lawful policy decisions and illegal activities.

government.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

government.title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.short_title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.plain_summary: Corruption affects how businesses are distributed across different industries. In Brazil, areas with higher levels of corruption tend to have fewer jobs and business establishments in sectors like construction and manufacturing. Instead, there's a larger presence of agricultural activities. The study also found that where corruption is more prevalent, the competition among businesses becomes tighter or less competitive depending on the sector.

government.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector: Policy Frameworks for Accountability, Ethics, and Human Rights Protection
government.short_title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector: Policy Frameworks for Accountability,…
government.plain_summary: This research examines how governments can manage artificial intelligence effectively while ensuring they're accountable for its decisions, follow ethical guidelines, and protect people's rights. It found that transparency, having someone supervise AI systems, and regular audits are important ways to hold AI accountable. Ethical principles like fairness and avoiding discrimination need to be followed more consistently than what policies promise. To keep privacy safe and ensure everyone has a say in how AI is used, it’s crucial for governments to have independent oversight bodies.

government.title: Building Village Financial Accountability through Transparency: The Role of Serial Mediators in Commitment and Integrity of Village Government Apparatus in South Sumatra Province
government.short_title: Building Village Financial Accountability through Transparency: The Role of Serial Mediators i…
government.source: Dinasti International Journal of Education Management and Social Science
government.plain_summary: This study examines how transparency affects financial accountability in villages in South Sumatra Province by looking at the roles of commitment and integrity among local government officials. It found that when villagers are more transparent about their finances, it leads to higher levels of commitment and integrity from officials. This, in turn, improves financial accountability within the village. However, there's no direct effect of transparency on financial accountability itself.

government.title: Risk-Based Reform of Anti-Money Laundering Criminal Law: Aligning Domestic Legal Frameworks with International Standards
government.short_title: Risk-Based Reform of Anti-Money Laundering Criminal Law: Aligning Domestic Legal Frameworks wi…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how Vietnam can improve its anti-money laundering (AML) laws to better fight money laundering. The study finds that while Vietnam has made progress in aligning its laws with international standards, there are still some weaknesses. For example, the current system relies too much on specific crimes as triggers for money laundering investigations. It also struggles with proving cases without direct evidence.

government.title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fiscal Digitization and E-Procurement Systems in Enhancing Administrative Transparency and Public Sector Integrity
government.short_title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fisca…
government.source: Science, Education and Innovations in the context of modern problems
government.plain_summary: Digital governance in Algeria has been adopted as a strategy to combat corruption, especially in sectors like taxation and procurement. The country is digitizing tax administration and implementing electronic public procurement systems, which have improved transparency and accountability. These digital tools help reduce discretionary practices, enhance traceability, and improve access to information for the public. However, there are still challenges such as incomplete integration of digital systems, cybersecurity issues, and uneven administrative capacity that need addressing.

government.title: Law Enforcement vs NGOs: How Do the Different Professional Backgrounds of Anti-Trafficking Practitioners Influence Their Views on Human Trafficking in the UK?
government.short_title: Law Enforcement vs NGOs: How Do the Different Professional Backgrounds of Anti-Trafficking Pra…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how different backgrounds of anti-human trafficking professionals—law enforcement officers versus support workers—affect their views on human trafficking in the UK. Law enforcement officials tend to see trafficking through a lens focused on public protection, often leading them to view traffickers as criminals and victims as potential threats. Support workers, however, focus more on understanding victims' needs and traumas, seeing them as vulnerable individuals who need help. These different perspectives can lead to stereotypes that don't fully capture the complexity of human trafficking situations.

government.title: Effectiveness of School-Based Anti-Drug Clubs in Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Drug Abuse Among Students in Basic Education Schools in Abuja Municipal Area Council, Nigeria
government.short_title: Effectiveness of School-Based Anti-Drug Clubs in Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Drug Abus…
government.source: Journal of Education Research and Library Practice
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how well anti-drug clubs work in schools to teach students about the dangers of using drugs. In Abuja, Nigeria, they surveyed 300 middle school students who were part of these clubs. The study found that these clubs are very effective in helping students understand why drug use is bad for their health and future. Students agreed that club activities helped them learn more about how drugs can affect their grades, friendships, laws, and mental health.

government.short_title: Exploring the Anti-Inflammatory Potential of Choerospondias axillaris Through Molecular Dockin…
government.source: Journal of Manmohan Memorial Institute of Health Sciences
government.plain_summary: This study compared hormone and bone health indicators between women before and after menopause. It found that postmenopausal women had higher thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels and alkaline phosphatase (ALP), along with lower calcium and phosphate in their blood. The research used various statistical methods to analyze these markers, including multivariate analysis and machine learning models like random forest which showed 81% accuracy in predicting menopausal status based on ALP and calcium levels. Age also influenced calcium levels more than menopause status did.

government.title: Unpacking the Emergence of Unqualified Audit Opinions as Quasi‐Accountability in Indonesian Public Sector
government.short_title: Unpacking the Emergence of Unqualified Audit Opinions as Quasi‐Accountability in Indonesian Pu…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how unqualified audit opinions (UAOs) are used in Indonesian local governments. Despite an increase in these opinions, they don't necessarily mean stronger accountability. Instead, their rise shows that audits support claims about government integrity and fighting corruption. Auditors play a key role here, balancing expectations from the environment with their own risks.

government.title: Political power and wealth distribution: how anti-corruption reforms reshape inequality
government.short_title: Political power and wealth distribution: how anti-corruption reforms reshape inequality
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how anti-corruption measures affect who gets rich from government actions. By using data from many countries, it found that when governments take steps to reduce corruption over time, the top earners don't get as much wealth anymore. At the same time, people at the bottom of the income ladder see a small increase in their share of total wealth. These changes happen gradually and last for years.

It mentions that many primary schools have problems like not adapting well to students' age or having too much formality. The author suggests using these places more practically by designing learning experiences where students can solve real problems and learn from their findings. This way, it helps students understand history better and feel connected to the past.

government.short_title: QUANTITATIVE ASSESSMENT OF THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ANTI-CORRUPTION STRATEGIES IN CANDIDATE COUNTR…
government.plain_summary: This research evaluates how well anti-corruption measures work in countries that are trying to join the European Union. It uses different methods like looking at reports from the EU, analyzing data, and comparing countries. The study found that some countries like Albania have strong law enforcement but others like Moldova show good progress over time. Ukraine is in the middle with both positive and negative aspects.

government.title: FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS OF ANTI-CRISIS MANAGEMENT IN THE DIGITAL AGE
government.short_title: FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS OF ANTI-CRISIS MANAGEMENT IN THE DIGITAL AGE
government.plain_summary: The article discusses how financial instruments used for crisis management have become crucial in ensuring stability and growth for organizations. In today's digital age, these instruments are combining traditional methods with innovative solutions like blockchain, crowdfunding, and risk forecasting to handle crises quickly and transparently. This has been particularly evident during the war in Ukraine where organizations have leveraged these tools to maintain liquidity, minimize losses, and attract more investors. However, challenges such as limited access to resources, high risks, and an inadequate legal environment still exist.

government.short_title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigati…
government.source: Journal of Public Policy and Local Government (JPPLG)
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how artificial intelligence is being used to help make decisions about climate and health issues in government. While this technology can be very useful, it also has the potential to unfairly treat certain groups of people if not managed properly. The paper introduces a new framework called AFCHG that helps governments use AI fairly when making these kinds of decisions. This framework includes four main parts: setting rules, ensuring fair decision-making processes, fixing any unfairness in how AI works, and considering fairness for all people.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.short_title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.plain_summary: E-government has become a way for governments to deliver services more efficiently and make governance transparent. However, implementing it can be challenging, especially in developing countries with limited resources. A case study from The Gambia found that while e-government helps improve service delivery, transparency, accountability, and citizen participation, there are still big hurdles like not having enough IT infrastructure or skilled employees to use digital tools effectively. There's also a lack of collaboration between different government departments and issues related to internet access and trust in government services.

government.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
government.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

government.short_title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION B…
government.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.

government.short_title: Working Paper 60: Understanding the enemy
government.source: Basel Institute on Governance Working Papers
government.plain_summary: This working paper discusses how corruption is not just about individual bad behavior but a networked issue involving social, economic, and political interactions. Understanding these networks can help in fighting corruption more effectively by seeing how they function across different levels of society. By looking at the structures and norms that support corrupt activities, we can develop better strategies to combat it. The paper suggests that anti-corruption efforts should learn from informal networks' positive aspects, making them a useful model for new initiatives.

government.title: The Impact of Corruption on Biodiversity Conservation in Nigeria: A Review of Some Critical Issues
government.short_title: The Impact of Corruption on Biodiversity Conservation in Nigeria: A Review of Some Critical Is…
government.source: International Journal of Governance and Public Policy Analysis
government.plain_summary: Corruption has significantly worsened the crisis of biodiversity loss and environmental degradation in Nigeria. It includes theft, bribery, fraud, abuse of power, and other unethical practices that harm natural resources like forests, wildlife habitats, and water bodies. This corruption leads to overexploitation of resources, deforestation, poaching, pollution, and many more issues. To address this crisis, reforms are needed in governance, legal systems, and institutions.

nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

nonprofit.plain_summary: This research examines how governments can manage artificial intelligence effectively while ensuring they're accountable for its decisions, follow ethical guidelines, and protect people's rights. It found that transparency, having someone supervise AI systems, and regular audits are important ways to hold AI accountable. Ethical principles like fairness and avoiding discrimination need to be followed more consistently than what policies promise. To keep privacy safe and ensure everyone has a say in how AI is used, it’s crucial for governments to have independent oversight bodies.

nonprofit.plain_summary: This article talks about how to use local historical sites related to the Red Army to teach kids about history. It mentions that many primary schools have problems like not adapting well to students' age or having too much formality. The author suggests using these places more practically by designing learning experiences where students can solve real problems and learn from their findings. This way, it helps students understand history better and feel connected to the past.

nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

nonprofit.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.
